corrected_value.title: Psychological Examining in the United States Army.

decisions.reason: In addition to replicating Stephen Jay Gould's (1981) undergraduate administration of the Army Beta (represented by shipped row input_row_index 1094 and blind target_index 0), the authors empirically re-analyze two original correlation matrices of World War I draftee Army Beta subtest scores (n = 693 on p. 390 and n = 1102 on p. 634) from Yerkes (1921, reference [15]: Yerkes R.M., 'Psychological Examining in the United States Army.', Government Printing Office, 1921) using confirmatory factor analysis (Tables 4 and 5) to test the robustness of the original test creators' claim that the Army Beta subtests measure a single general cognitive ability against a two-factor alternative separating subtests with written numbers. Yerkes (1921) is the primary historical psychometric report of the World War I Army testing program and is completely distinct from Gould's book (the sole shipped row, input_row_index 1094); report equivalence does not apply. No prior adjudication or state file exists.
